headline: Segment declines and divestiture charges widen net loss
summary_short: Net sales fell 10.5% y/y to $2,265M as gross margin compressed across all three segments; a $182M loss on the pending Glass Reinforcements sale pushed the net loss attributable to Owens Corning to $105M.
summary_long: Net sales fell 10.5% y/y to $2,265M on lower volumes across all three segments (Roofing -14%, Insulation -3%, Doors -12%), with gross margin down $215M on volume, pricing, and input-cost inflation. Segment EBITDA fell in Roofing (-$101M), Insulation (-$58M) and Doors (-$34M); Corporate costs rose $79M on higher restructuring and a larger Paroc marine-recall liability. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations was $369M versus $565M. The repriced Glass Reinforcements sale produced a $182M pre-tax loss in discontinued operations, widening the net loss attributable to Owens Corning to $105M from $93M. Cash fell to $272M and equity to $3,644M; the company guides FY2026 general corporate expenses to $245M-$255M.

drivers.explanation: GAAP results were pressured by lower volumes across all three segments and by a $182M pre-tax loss on the repriced Glass Reinforcements divestiture (booked in discontinued operations), while Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations fell to $369M from $565M.
Net sales fell $265M as lower volumes across Roofing, Insulation and Doors were only partly offset by favorable mix; selling prices were also lower in all three segments.
Not broken out separately, but the release ties gross-margin compression to production downtime and input-cost inflation raising unit costs, alongside the volume decline.
Gross margin fell $215M on lower volumes across all segments, lower selling prices, production downtime, and input-cost inflation.

Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations fell to $369M from $565M; segment EBITDA declined in Roofing, Insulation and Doors while Corporate costs rose $79M on higher restructuring and the Paroc liability.
Operating income fell on the same volume, price, downtime and cost-inflation pressures cited for gross margin, plus other expense rising to $95M from $22M on restructuring and the Paroc recall.
Pretax income fell with operating income; net interest expense was roughly flat at $66M versus $64M, driven by lower interest income on lower cash balances.
Net income fell with pretax income and a higher effective tax rate (28% versus 26%), reflecting state and local taxes, foreign tax effects, and changes in unrecognized tax benefits.
Basic EPS combines $0.47 of continuing-operations earnings per share with a $(1.77) discontinued-operations loss per share tied to the Glass Reinforcements divestiture.
Diluted EPS mirrors basic, combining $0.47 of continuing-operations earnings per share with a $(1.76) discontinued-operations loss per share from the divestiture.
Operating cash outflow widened by $105M, primarily on lower cash earnings, partly offset by the change in working capital.
Cash paid for property, plant and equipment was higher, a driver of the $31M increase in cash used in investing activities, alongside lower proceeds from asset sales.
Cash and cash equivalents from continuing operations fell to $272M, consistent with the wider operating cash outflow and dividends paid in the quarter.
Equity fell on the net loss attributable to Owens Corning and $65M of dividends declared during the quarter, per the statement of changes in equity.
Share count fell y/y mainly from 2025 treasury-stock purchases; the company repurchased no shares in the current quarter.
